ei.title: There’s More than One Way to Vote
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: We make many personal choices in our lives, from who to have lunch with to what career to pursue. However, there are many situations where we must make decisions as a group. Group decision-making is not as simple as our personal choices, as it involves numerous voices with differing opinions. Voting is often used to make group decisions fairer and more efficient, and various voting methods have been developed over time. The following story illustrates how these different voting methods work. The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need. Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions. So they decided to put it to a vote. When they asked for advice from Ms. Akers, the council’s advisor, she encouraged them not to use the familiar voting method, but to try something different instead. After doing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method. The entire council was curious to find out if the different methods would yield different results. On the day of the vote, each possible event was given a letter: “art show” was represented by the letter A, the letter B indicated “bake sale,” and C stood for “charity concert.” Each of the 20 council members was given a voting slip and instructed to write down the options in order of preference. For example, if the charity concert was their first choice, followed by the bake sale and the art show, they would write CBA. After every member had voted, the voting slips were counted. The results were as follows: The First-Past-The-Post Method The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods. Voters are given several options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes wins. Neither the second nor third preference matters at all, so they are ignored. This method is commonly used in political elections around the world. The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7. The FPTP method is uncomplicated and easy to understand, but it has a significant weakness. It is possible to win a vote without the support of the majority. That was the case here. According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to hold a charity concert. However, only 8 out of 20 council members chose the charity concert as their first preference, which equaled 40% of the total votes. The Alternative Vote Method Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting. For an option to win in the first round, it needs to get more than 50% of the first-preference votes. As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting was required. Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it. Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences. As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total. This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9. As a result, the bake sale would be the winner. Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either. It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes. In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received. The Condorcet Method Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method involves comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options. In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C. Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB. Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9. They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9. As option A, the art show, was preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner. The Condorcet method’s weakness is that, along with being complex, it sometimes fails to select a winner. This is especially true in elections that contain numerous options. It is possible that no option will be clearly preferred over the others. Instead of all methods pointing toward a single option and making the council’s choice easier, the winner differed with each method. After a long, intense discussion with Ms. Akers, the student council members decided to choose the Condorcet method, as they liked the idea of directly comparing each option with the others. Everyone agreed that they learned a lot about different voting systems through this experience. It is obvious that choosing an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task. No voting system is flawless or clearly superior to another. Whichever we choose will have pros and cons. Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not ranking our choices at all. Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, arguing that more complex methods deliver more accurate results. All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make better decisions as a society. Ultimately, understanding all of the possible voting methods and weighing their pros and cons allows us to better understand the process of decision-making. When we understand decision-making better, we are more likely to become better decision-makers ourselves.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② get → gets: whichever(어느 것이든)는 단수 취급이므로 단수 동사 gets
det.analysis:

✅ ④ ignored: so they are ignored에서 '무시되는' 대상이라 수동태 과거분사로 적절
det.tip: whichever + 단수동사(gets): '어느 것이든 ~하는 것'은 하나로 취급

✅ ④ fairer: 투표는 집단 결정을 더 '공정하게' 만든다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: differing opinions(서로 다른 의견) ↔ agreeing(동의하는)

det.korean: ② easy → challenging: 이상적 투표 방식을 고르는 것은 복잡하고 '까다로운(challenging)' 일
det.analysis:
✅ ① learned: 서로 다른 투표 제도에 대해 많이 '배웠다'는 문맥에 적절
❌ ② easy(쉬운) → challenging(까다로운): 앞의 complex(복잡한)와 나란히 이어져 '이상적 투표 방식을 고르는 것은 복잡하고 까다로운 일'이라는 뜻이므로 challenging이 맞다. complex와 easy는 서로 모순되어 부적절 ← 정답
✅ ③ accurate: 더 복잡한 방식이 더 '정확한' 결과를 낸다는 주장에 적절
✅ ④ better: 더 '나은' 결정을 하도록 돕는다는 글의 결론에 적절
det.tip: complex and challenging(복잡하고 까다로운) — complex와 짝이 되는 말은 easy가 아니라 challenging

❌ ④ the advisor's approval(조언자의 승인): 본문에 없는 내용

det.korean: 빈칸에 a greater influence(더 큰 영향력)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① a smaller role(더 작은 역할): AV의 약점을 지적하는 흐름과 반대

❌ ④ an equal weight(동등한 비중): '더 큰' 영향을 강조하는 문맥과 맞지 않음

As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total.  This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9.  As a result, the bake sale would be the winner.  Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either.  It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes.  In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: AV 2차 집계와 그 결과.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 본문 'option B had 11 total votes ~ the bake sale would be the winner'와 일치 ← 정답
❌ ② 본문 'Option A ~ received the fewest first-preference votes ~ was eliminated'에서 A는 가장 적은 표를 받아 탈락했으므로 불일치
❌ ③ 본문 'redistributed based on their second preferences'에서 1순위가 아니라 '2순위'에 따라 재분배되었으므로 불일치
❌ ④ 본문 'the AV method is not perfect either'에서 AV도 완벽하지 않다고 했으므로 불일치
det.tip: 탈락 표는 2순위(second preferences) 기준 재분배. AV도 완벽하지 않습니다.

ch: AV 2차 집계 결과 빵 판매(B)가 11표로 최종 승자가 되었다.
예술 전시회(A)는 가장 많은 1순위 표를 받아 그대로 유지되었다.
탈락한 A안의 표는 유권자들의 1순위 선호에 따라 재분배되었다.
AV 방식은 언제나 완벽하고 공정한 결과를 보장한다.

questions.passage: Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, with only 5 council members ①<u>voting</u> for it. Therefore, option A was ②<u>eliminated</u>, and the 5 members' votes were ③<u>redistributed</u> based on their second preferences. As a result, 4 votes for option B and 1 vote for option C ④<u>was</u> added to the total.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ was → were: 주어가 '4 votes ~ and 1 vote'로 복수이므로 복수 동사 were
det.analysis:
✅ ① voting: 'with only 5 council members voting for it(5명만이 그것에 투표한 채로)'에서 'with + 목적어 + -ing' 분사구문으로 적절
✅ ② eliminated: option A was eliminated(A안이 탈락되었다) 수동태로 적절
✅ ③ redistributed: the votes were redistributed(표가 재분배되었다) 수동태로 적절
❌ ④ was → were: '4 votes for option B and 1 vote for option C ___ added to the total'에서 진짜 주어는 '4표 …그리고 1표'로 둘을 더한 복수다. 따라서 복수 동사 were가 맞다 ← 정답
det.tip: A and B로 이어진 주어는 복수 → were added

questions.passage: Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it.  Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences.  As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, AV 방식에서 A안이 탈락한 뒤 그 표들이 '무엇'에 근거하여 재분배되었는지 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 탈락 표의 재분배 기준.
det.analysis: 본문 'the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences.'에서 탈락한 A안의 표들이 유권자들의 '2순위 선호(second preferences)'에 근거해 재분배되었다고 밝혔다.
det.tip: based on their second preferences(2순위 선호에 근거하여)에서 second preferences를 찾습니다.

questions.passage: Instead of all methods pointing toward a single option and making the council’s choice easier, the winner differed with each method.  After a long, intense discussion with Ms.  Akers, the student council members decided to choose the Condorcet method, as they liked the idea of directly comparing each option with the others.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 오랜 논의 끝에 학생회 구성원들이 최종적으로 선택하기로 결정한 투표 방식의 이름을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 학생회가 최종 선택한 방식.
det.analysis: 본문 'the student council members decided to choose the Condorcet method, as they liked the idea of directly comparing each option with the others.'에서 학생회는 각 선택지를 직접 비교한다는 점이 마음에 들어 'Condorcet' 방식을 최종적으로 선택하기로 했다.
det.tip: decided to choose the Condorcet method(Condorcet 방식을 선택하기로 결정)에서 Condorcet을 찾습니다.

questions.passage: Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not __________ (rank) our choices at all. Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: ranking (동명사).
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'by not ___ our choices'에서 by는 '~함으로써'라는 뜻의 전치사다. 전치사 뒤에는 동사를 그대로 쓸 수 없고 동명사(-ing)로 바꿔 써야 한다. 따라서 rank를 ranking으로 바꿔야 한다. not은 동명사 앞에 붙어 '~하지 않음으로써'가 된다.
det.tip: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사: by not ranking(순위를 매기지 않음으로써)

questions.passage: We make many personal choices in our lives, from who to have lunch with to what career to pursue.  However, there are many situations where we must make decisions as a group.  Group decision-making is not as simple as our personal choices, as it involves numerous voices with differing opinions.  Voting is often used to make group decisions fairer and more efficient, and various voting methods have been developed over time.  The following story illustrates how these different voting methods work.  The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need.  Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions.  So they decided to put it to a vote.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체를 아우르는 중심 소재.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 학생회 사례를 통해 FPTP·AV·Condorcet 세 투표 방식이 어떻게 작동하고 각각 어떤 장단점이 있는지 설명하는 것이 글 전체의 주제 ← 정답
❌ ② 자선 콘서트 선택은 하나의 예시일 뿐 주제가 아님
❌ ③ FPTP가 늘 우수하다는 내용은 본문과 반대(각 방식마다 약점이 있음)
❌ ④ 방식마다 결과가 달랐으므로 '늘 1순위를 반영한다'는 것은 사실과 반대
det.tip: 세 가지 투표 방식과 그 장단점이 글 전체를 관통합니다.

ch: 집단의 의사결정을 위한 여러 투표 방식과 각 방식의 특징 및 장단점
학생회가 기금 마련 행사로 자선 콘서트를 최종 선택하게 된 과정
FPTP 방식이 다른 두 방식보다 언제나 우수한 이유
투표 결과가 항상 유권자의 1순위 선호를 그대로 반영하는 원리

questions.passage: We make many personal choices in our lives, from who to have lunch with to what career to pursue.  However, there are many situations where we must make decisions as a group.  Group decision-making is not as simple as our personal choices, as it involves numerous voices with differing opinions.  Voting is often used to make group decisions fairer and more efficient, and various voting methods have been developed over time.  The following story illustrates how these different voting methods work.  The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need.  Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions.  So they decided to put it to a vote.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글쓴이가 전하려는 핵심 메시지.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 가장 단순한 FPTP도 약점이 있으므로 '늘 가장 공정하다'는 요지와 반대
✅ ② 본문 'No voting system is flawless ~ understanding all of the possible voting methods and weighing their pros and cons allows us to ~ make better decisions'와 통하는 핵심 메시지 ← 정답
❌ ③ 글은 집단 의사결정 방식을 다루며 개인 선택 우선을 주장하지 않음
❌ ④ 참여율에 관한 내용은 본문에 없음
det.tip: 완벽한 제도는 없다 + 장단점을 이해하면 더 나은 결정을 한다 = 요지

ch: 가장 단순한 투표 방식이 언제나 가장 공정한 결과를 낳는다.
완벽한 투표 제도는 없으므로 여러 방식의 장단점을 이해하는 것이 더 나은 결정으로 이어진다.
집단의 결정보다 개인의 선택이 언제나 우선되어야 한다.
투표 방식이 복잡할수록 학생들의 참여율이 낮아진다.

questions.passage: The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need.  Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions.  So __________.  When they asked for advice from Ms.  Akers, the council’s advisor, she encouraged them not to use the familiar voting method, but to try something different instead.  After doing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'그래서 그들은 그것을 투표에 부치기로 결정했다.'

[조건]
(1) a, decided, it, put, they, to, to, vote 를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: they decided to put it to a vote
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- they(주어) + decided(동사): 그들은 결정했다
- decide 뒤에는 to부정사를 목적어로 쓴다: decided + to + put(놓기로 결정했다)
- 'put A to a vote'는 'A를 투표에 부치다'라는 굳어진 표현이다: put + it + to + a + vote
- 순서대로 놓으면 they / decided / to / put / it / to / a / vote
det.tip: decide to + 동사원형 / put ~ to a vote(~을 투표에 부치다)

questions.wa: they decided to put it to a vote
accept: they decided to put it to a vote
